headerBody: Vietnam: Tourist Scams documents 66 specific scams across Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Hoi An, Ha Long Bay and 7 more destinations — each verified against Vietnamese police (113) bulletins, the VNAT tourism authority and VCCA consumer agency, VnExpress and Tuoi Tre News reporting, r/VietNam threads, and verified local news. Not a recycled blog list.
quadHead: Four ways Vietnam catches tourists off guard.

quad.title: The Noi Bai Fake-Grab
quad.tl: A man in arrivals flashes a phone screen that looks like Grab and claims to be your driver — the plate never matches the app, and the Old Quarter ride bills at 1,200,000 VND instead of the real ~300,000 VND.

quad.title: The 'Italian Wool' Tailor
quad.tl: A tout's tea and a design chat lead to a 'partner' shop where 30 USD/metre cotton is sold as 90 USD/metre 'Italian wool,' rush-built in 24 hours and stitched to fail after one wash.

quad.title: The Clone Cruise Site
quad.tl: Lookalike domains mimic Bhaya, Paradise and Indochina Sails with 'exclusive' pricing; you wire from home, get a polished PDF, then reach the Tuan Chau pier to find no booking in the system.

quad.title: The Bui Vien Hostess Bar
quad.tl: A 'friendly local' steers you to a side-street bar off Bui Vien; a hostess joins, drinks have no posted price, then a 4,000,000+ VND bill lands while bouncers stand at the exit.

body: Vietnam: Tourist Scams is part of the tabiji.ai Travel Safety Series. Every scam is documented against Vietnamese sources — the police (113) and the national emergency lines (113 police, 114 fire, 115 ambulance), the VNAT tourism authority and the VCCA consumer agency — plus VnExpress and Tuoi Tre News reporting, r/VietNam threads, and verified local news. Sourced, not recycled.

66 specific scams across Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Hoi An, Ha Long Bay, Da Nang, Hue, Nha Trang, Sapa and more. The exact scripts, the red flags that give them away, and the Vietnamese phrases that shut them down — written so you can show them on your phone.
Scams evolve, so the book is re-researched every year, and the current edition sits in your Kindle library. Built for the traveler who wants to move through Vietnam relaxed, not braced.
